question.problem: Consider the function $g(x,y)={x}^{y}.$ What is the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction in which the function increases most rapidly?
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

In our case, we compute $∇g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{y}),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{y})⟩ \\  & =⟨y{x}^{y-1},\,{x}^{y}\operatorname{ln}⁡x⟩ \\ ∇\,g(1,1) & =⟨(1){1}^{1-1},\,({1}^{1})\operatorname{ln}⁡1⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,1)$ in the direction of $∇g(1,1)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}‖∇\,g(1,1)‖ & =‖⟨1,0⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
